topic: The Global Spread of the Potato

text.content: Today, the potato is one of the most common foods in the world, but it originally came from only one place. The plant first grew high up in the cold, harsh environment of South America. Because the edible part of the plant grows safely underground, it could survive freezing temperatures that destroyed other crops. The first farmers to successfully grow this reliable food source lived in a famous South American mountain range. This area is known as the Andes mountains.

In the 1500s, European ships arrived in South America. When these ships returned home, they brought the potato with them. The people who first brought the plant across the ocean to Europe were Spanish explorers. However, European farmers did not want to eat it at first. Because the potato grows underground and looks strange, many people incorrectly believed that the plant was poisonous.

It took more than a hundred years for the potato to become popular in Europe. Eventually, national leaders realized that a farmer could grow a huge amount of potatoes on a very small piece of land. It provided far more food than traditional crops like wheat. Because poor families finally had enough calories to survive the winter, the potato caused a massive increase in the population of Europe during the 1700s and 1800s.

However, relying on a single type of food can be very dangerous. By the 1840s, the people of Ireland ate almost nothing but potatoes. Suddenly, the entire harvest was destroyed by a dangerous plant disease. This disease was called potato blight. Because there was no other food available, over a million people died of hunger, and another million were forced to leave the country.

Despite the disaster in Ireland, the potato continued to spread around the globe. Today, it is grown in almost every country on Earth. It is an incredibly important part of the modern global food supply because it requires very little water and can grow in poor soil. From a wild mountain plant, it has successfully become the fourth largest food crop in the world.

stage_3_logic.instructions: Are the following statements True, False, or Not Given according to the text?

questions.prompt: European farmers immediately started eating potatoes as soon as they arrived from South America.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B states that 'European farmers did not want to eat it at first' because they thought it was poisonous.

questions.prompt: The potato caused a massive population increase in Europe because it provided more food on a small piece of land than wheat.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C confirms that it provided more food than wheat on a small piece of land, giving poor families enough calories to survive.

questions.prompt: Today, China grows more potatoes than any other country in the world.
questions.explanation: Paragraph E mentions that the potato is grown in almost every country, but it never specifies which country grows the most.
